trigger: an agent re-registers (for example an agent restart or upgrade) while the heartbeat reconcile is reading the rule and Baseline stores, so the rules built for the old session are sent by agent id to the new session
classification_rationale: the flow did not compare the session it prepared the push for with the session that receives it
summary: Fixed in cbe362459. The per-finding reporter was not given to the ledger writer, so it is recorded as orchestrator, and no agent re-review of cbe362459 is recorded in this fragment (the ledger writer read its diff). Impact reasoning from the code at 99416c97b: the push is built from the session OS and from the identity fields the scope check reads (AgentRegistry::evaluate_scope_for_agent), while send_push_ delivers by agent id to whatever session exists at send time, so a re-registration with a changed attribute would deliver a rule set filtered for the old session under the fresh generation label and the agent would report converged. Wrong result presented as correct (I3) under a race (E5) derives HIGH, BLOCKING. The orchestrator expected MEDIUM or lower; the derivation does not support that, because the wrong outcome is not proven unable to occur (no E6). The fix: GuardianReconcileFlow Deps.session_id is required (the constructor rejects an empty callable), the session id is read before the OS and again just before the send, and a mismatch withholds the push, increments yuzu_server_guardian_reconciles_total{result="no_session"}, keeps the claim and writes no audit row. Tests in tests/unit/server/test_guardian_reconcile_flow.cpp: a re-registration during the load sends nothing and counts no_session while an unchanged session still sends, and a null session_id is rejected at construction. The same commit corrects the LIFETIME comment in guardian_reconcile_flow.hpp (custom_properties_store_ is declared below heartbeat_ingestion_ and is safe only through ServerImpl::stop() order) and adds the parsed_scope null guard in guardian_push_fn_ (return -1 instead of dereferencing an empty optional). Residual, stated in the code comment and not closed: a re-registration that lands after the second session read and before the send is not detected. No issue is filed for that residual.
